title: Python aborts at exit in gates; macOS shows crash dialogs
what: Python 3.14 processes started by Python (parent process Python) abort with SIGABRT at interpreter shutdown: fatal_error in _enter_buffered_busy from _io__Buffered_close, the "could not acquire lock for <_io.BufferedWriter name='<stderr>'> at interpreter shutdown, possibly due to daemon threads" case. A daemon thread is still writing to stdout or stderr when the program exits. Find which relay program or test does this (the crashes came in bursts while gates ran, 16:39-16:43 local), stop the daemon thread or join it before exit, and add a check that no gate run leaves a new Python .ips crash report. Also 3 bash SIGSEGV reports the same day: check whether they share the cause.
why: Each abort opens a macOS "Python quit unexpectedly. Click Reopen ... Report" window in front of the owner; 25 on 30 Oct, 1 on 29 Oct.
failing_case: ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports has 25 Python-2026-10-30-*.ips reports, 19 of the last 30 being EXC_CRASH SIGABRT "Abort trap: 6" with the triggered thread in _enter_buffered_busy / _io__Buffered_close; the owner sees the macOS dialog "Click Reopen to open the application again. Click Report ..." again and again.
pass_cases: a full relay gate run leaves no new Python-*.ips report in ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports
the program found as the cause exits without the fatal error when a daemon thread is mid-write (a test reproduces the abort before the fix)

said: Click Reopen to open the application again. Click Report to see more detailed information and send a report to Apple
Откуда, это появляется раз за разом

fact: 30 Oct, owner answered "a" to: turn the macOS crash dialogs off now and back on after the fix. The front ran `defaults write com.apple.CrashReporter DialogType none` (before: key not set). Crash reports still go to ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports. When this item lands, turn the dialog back on: `defaults delete com.apple.CrashReporter DialogType` (restores the default).

30 Oct, cause found and reproduced: the crash reports show a second thread "Thread-1 (watch_stdin)" blocked in sys.stdin.buffer.read. watch_stdin is in lib/relay_gate_remote.py:171 on the unlanded branch wt/gates-on-the-vps-hosts-transport-watch-b (VPS gates, changes 3-4), not on master; its tests ran under that branch's gates. A minimal script with a daemon thread in sys.stdin.buffer.read(4096) exits SIGABRT (134) on Python 3.14; with os.read(0, 4096) it exits 0. Fix: watch_stdin uses os.read(0, 4096), plus a test that runs the program with an open stdin pipe and a normal end and asserts exit 0. The fix goes into the VPS change before it lands; this item closes when that change lands with the test (then the crash dialog is turned back on).
